evals.name: object-page-great-wave
evals.prompt: Build the object page for Hokusai's Great Wave for the Edo unit of the F1 'Histories of making' course, as one self-contained HTML file (inline CSS, no build step). Use the image at /home/claude/creative-world/modules/F1-histories-of-making/build/units/edo/public/img/hi-wave.webp (copy it next to the HTML as hi-wave.webp and reference it relatively). Facts to use: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, JP1847, 'Under the Wave off Kanagawa (Kanagawa oki nami ura)', from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, c. 1830–32, woodblock print, ink and colour on paper, 25.7 × 37.9 cm, CC0; publisher Nishimuraya Yohachi (Eijudō); the Met's spectroscopy found Prussian blue mixed with indigo in the dark stripes of the wave and pure Prussian blue, printed twice, in the hollow; the sky's pink was safflower and faded first; the title cartouche and the signature 'Hokusai aratame Iitsu hitsu' sit top left; three boats carry fish to Edo's market; Mount Fuji is small under the wave; about 8,000 impressions is the usual estimate (probable, Korenberg); 111 impressions located by 2020, 113 by 2024; no blocks survive. The page should read as part of the course and work at 1440 px and 390 px. Then take screenshots at both widths with Playwright (require('/home/claude/creative-world/modules/F1-histories-of-making/build/lectures/node_modules/playwright'), executablePath '/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome') and save them beside the HTML.
evals.expected_output: index.html + hi-wave.webp + two screenshots; an annotated object page in the course's finish

evals.name: atlas-lecture-panel
evals.prompt: Design the Atlas of Making's world view for the F1 'Histories of making' course with Lecture 5 'Blue' selected, as a static HTML mock at 1440 × 900 (inline CSS; a schematic globe is fine, drawn as SVG circles and a few arcs; no map libraries). It needs: a left list of the nine world chapters with counts (F1.6 Africa 41, F1.7 The Americas 58, F1.8 East Asia 120, F1.9 South and Southeast Asia 44, F1.9a West Asia before Islam 37, F1.10 The Islamic world 66, F1.11 Europe and the Mediterranean 150, F1.12 Oceania 18, F1.12a The Arctic 9), the East Asia chapter expanded to its eight Edo lectures (L1 A city of a million, L2 Four hands one sheet, L3 Colour calendars poets, L4 The publisher, L5 Blue, L6 The ban and the road, L7 Afterlife, L8 Money); the globe in the middle with the route Berlin → Amsterdam → the Cape → Batavia → Nagasaki → Edo for the selected lecture and every other route dimmed; and a right panel for Lecture 5 with: the title, a one-line deck ('A European pigment's price curve, 1704–1831'), a paragraph (write 80–120 words from these facts: Prussian blue was made in Berlin around 1704 by accident; it reached Japan only through Nagasaki by Dutch ship; from 1824 Chinese junks undercut the Dutch and the Nagasaki price fell from 87 to 31 monme a kin by 1828; in 1829 an all-blue fan started a fad; at New Year 1831 Eijudō advertised Hokusai's Fuji series in the new blue), relations ('read in: F1.8 East Asia', 'shares routes with: F1.13 Networks', 'appears in: Act II, scenes 3–4'), two figures (1704–1831; 87 → 31 monme), sources (Smith, 'Prussian blue'; Fitzhugh; Korenberg), and previous / next (L4, L6). Save as index.html and take a 1440 × 900 screenshot with Playwright (require('/home/claude/creative-world/modules/F1-histories-of-making/build/lectures/node_modules/playwright'), executablePath '/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome') beside it.
evals.expected_output: index.html + screenshot; a list · globe · panel layout in the course's finish

evals.name: seals-typology-and-eras-span-list
evals.prompt: Make one HTML page (inline CSS, self-contained) with two components for the Edo unit of the F1 'Histories of making' course. First, a typology plate of the censor's seals on Edo prints: four classes in rows: 'No seal required' 1600–1790; 'The kiwame seal 極' 1790–1843 (a round seal cut into the key block); 'Named censors' seals' 1843–1853 (one headman's name seal 1843–1847, then two from 1847); 'Aratame 改 and a date seal' 1853–1876 (a round aratame seal with a zodiac year-month date seal). Draw the seals as simple SVG marks (circles and squares with the characters 極, 改 and a placeholder name), one shelf per row, a date range under each seal, a note that the margin dates the sheet. Second, a span list of the six eras of the unit: A city is made 1603–1657; Black ink to colour 1657–1765; The golden age, under a censor 1765–1806; Blue and the road 1806–1842; The ban and the opening 1842–1868; The afterlife 1868–2024. The page should read as part of the course and work at 1440 px and 390 px; take screenshots at both widths with Playwright (require('/home/claude/creative-world/modules/F1-histories-of-making/build/lectures/node_modules/playwright'), executablePath '/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome') and save them beside the HTML.
evals.expected_output: index.html + two screenshots; a typology plate and a span list in the course's finish
